message.content: Lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) belong to very different families—Felidae (big cats) and Equidae (horses, zebras, donkeys). Their most recent common ancestor is not a specific species but a higher‑level clade. Both are part of the super‑order **Laurasiatheria**, which is itself a subgroup of the placental mammals (Eutheria). So, the common ancestor of a lion and a zebra is the ancestral lineage that gave rise to the Laurasiatherian mammals, dating back roughly 70–80 million years ago.
